chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: A man comes to me with dirhams, and I buy them from him with dinars. Then I give him a pouch containing dinars greater than the value of his dirhams. I say to him: From these dinars, such-and-such dinars are the price of your dirhams. So he takes the pouch from me, then returns it to me and says: Keep them recorded with you for me.
So he عليه السلام said: If the pouch contains sufficient amount to cover the price of his dirhams, then there is no harm in it.

key_terms.ثَمَنُ: the price or value assigned in the sale transaction
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no legal objection or prohibition in it
key_terms.كِيساً: a pouch containing the dinars handed over in the exchange
key_terms.وَفَاءٌ: sufficiency or adequacy to fully cover the owed amount
key_terms.ٱلدَّرَاهِمُ: silver coins being exchanged in the transaction
key_terms.ٱلدَّنَانِيرِ: gold coins used as the price for the dirhams

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh to exchange dirhams for dinars and then leave the dinars with the exchanger?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a currency-exchange transaction involving dirhams and dinars, followed by leaving the exchanged amount in the seller's custody. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام permits it on the condition that the pouch actually contains enough dinars to fulfill the stated price of the dirhams. The narration relates to the validity of exchange and entrusted retention in financial dealings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4039 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (as): "A man comes to me with dirhams, and I buy them from him with dinars. Then I give him a pouch containing more dinars than the value of his dirhams.
I say to him: 'From these dinars, such and such amount is the price of your dirhams.'
He takes the pouch from me, then returns it and says: 'Keep it with you for me.'"
Imam (as) said: "If the pouch contains enough to cover the value of his dirhams, then there is no harm in it."
